items.title: Harness Engineering 2.0 is here!
items.summary:
Harness Engineering 2.0 is here!

We benchmark models all the time but the harness running the model can dramatically improve the result, cost, and execution time too.

And finally, devs just open-sourced Harness Arena, where you can test the same task across multiple harness and model combinations side by side.

You provide one task and then run it across several model x harness configs that you want to test.

Every config receives the same prompt, files, tools, skills, and evaluation checks. Harness Arena then returns:

- total cost
- execution time
- whether the task passed
- files and artifacts produced

If you want to try it yourself, it is implemented within the open-source HarnessRouter project.

Here's the repo: https://t.co/4y6zJShKSu

(don't forget to star it ⭐ )

HarnessRouter is a plug-and-play infrastructure layer that lets you run any harness under a single interface, like:

- Codex
- Hermes
- Claude code
- DeepSeek Harness
- System One, powered by Jev
- And 25 more agent harnesses

In Harness Arena, the cheapest run does not automatically win.

A config must complete the task correctly first. Cost and execution time are compared only among the configurations that pass.

Here's the result from one Harness Arena test:

- Hermes + GPT-5.2: 5/5 successful runs using 0.47 credits
- Claude Code + Opus 4.8: 3/5 successful runs using 223 credits

That is around 474x difference in credits, while the more expensive configuration also failed two runs.

You can keep the model fixed to measure how much the harness changes the result. Or vary both to find the best harness and model pairing for that task.

This helps answer practical questions such as:

- Should this task run on Codex or Claude?
- Can a cheaper config still pass every check?
- Which setup is best to handle this workload?

Once you find the best config, you can run future tasks through it using the same Unified Harness Protocol (UHP) interface for sessions, streaming, files, artifacts, cancellation, and failures.

So you are no longer choosing an agent stack based only on a model leaderboard.

Instead, you can benchmark the complete runtime on the task your product actually needs to solve.

To dive deeper, my co-founder wrote an article explaining why model routing is different from harness routing, how UHP works, and what supporting multiple agent runtimes involves.

It also covers the local setup, a working request, and how sessions and files move through the system.

Read it below.

items.title: The BSO Meets AI, and Explores the Vitality of Classical Music Today | The Harvard Crimson
items.summary:
At the center of Machover’s composition philosophy is his belief that classical music finds a natural extension and innovation in technology. He revealed in an interview with GBH music that the music he hears in his head is often beyond the scope of traditional instruments. Thus, alongside the MIT Media Lab, Machover has developed an audio AI that takes in the playing of the orchestra as input and produces live synthetic sounds that — as Machover puts it — “enhances” the orchestra. [...] From Oct. 22 to 24, the Boston Symphony Orchestra and conductor Kent Nagano performed “already and not yet: A world premiere by Tod Machover.” The headliner was a modern classical work: an onstage musical dialogue between the BSO and a live AI system. Beyond the philosophical implications of the concept, the performance struck at a key nerve of classical music culture — a delicate balancing of tradition and relevance. [...] The piece was divided into three movements. The first movement, “SMASH UP,” was, in Machover’s words, a “clash/crisis” without audible enhancement from the AI.

The second, “WAKE UP,” was an “awakening”: the AI slowly produced sound in response to various solo lines in the orchestra. Then the last movement, “STAND UP,” was a “depiction of democracy,” as the musicians and AI listened to one another and negotiated the final musical product.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 leads scientific visual reasoning benchmark VIALS-AA; it makes more tool calls than any other Anthropic
items.summary:
Claude Fable 5.2 leads scientific visual reasoning benchmark VIALS-AA; it makes more tool calls than any other Anthropic model, unlike OpenAI models which make fewer as they get smarter

VIALS-AA is our implementation of @joinHandshakeAI’s VIALS benchmark for visual reasoning in life sciences research, across artifacts such as gel blots, plasmid maps, and phylogenies. Claude Fable 5.2 (max with fallback) scores 67% on VIALS-AA, ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (high) at 64% and GPT-6 Astra (max) at 63%. Fable averages ~37 tool calls per task, while Astra averages ~8, the fewest of any model we’ve tested.

On turn 4 of this protein interaction task, Fable creates crops and asks to view them. On turn 10, it builds a color mask by thresholding color channels. On turn 17, it fits a circle to each arc and unrolls the arc into a straight strip. On turn 31, it counts the bars as peaks in an intensity profile. And on turn 41, it maps every detected spoke back on the original image to check its work. Fable batches calls on 28 of its 51 turns, averaging 1.75 tool calls per turn, compared with 1.12 for Sonnet 5.5.

items.title: NVIDIA released a new RL framework:
items.summary:
NVIDIA released a new RL framework:

Your entire setup is one Python file:

- write a class with a step() function
- return a reward from it
- the framework handles the rest, up to 1T-class MoE training

In a typical RL framework, the environment and reward logic are added inside the trainer's codebase.

Adding a new task requires writing framework code, registering it, and wiring up config for it.

The reward usually comes from a separately trained reward model, which needs its own GPUs and placement next to the actor and critic.

NVIDIA's Molt framework drops both these requirements.

Every run takes an agent_path flag pointing to one Python module, and the trainer code never changes.

The module gives you two ways to plug in an agent.

> The first is an Env class where you write a step() function that receives the model's output and returns a reward, and the framework handles everything else, i.e., calling the model, tokenizing, and looping turn after turn until the episode ends.

> The second is a ChatAgent class, for agents that already exist as their own loop. Here, you write the loop yourself, calling the model through a standard OpenAI or Anthropic client, and the framework spins up a local server so those calls hit its vLLM engines instead of an external API.

Either way, the trainer sees the same thing, i.e., a trajectory of tokens and a reward at the end.

That reward can come from a string-match grader, code executed in a sandboxed subprocess, or an LLM-as-judge call.

So there is no reward model to train or place, and no environment code living inside the framework.

Under the hood, Molt runs a single trainable actor (plus an optional critic for PPO) on FSDP2, vLLM engines for rollout, and Ray queues between them, so generation, training, and weight sync overlap instead of running in lockstep.

Scaling just requires setting some flags on the same command.

The framework also splits the model across GPUs for you, so the script that trains an 8B model on one node can also train DeepSeek-V3-scale MoE models on a cluster by raising the parallelism flags.

Here's the repo: https://t.co/TafSfatER5

Since the framework is new, I am still experimenting with it and will share more about my learnings soon.

To dive deeper into how top AI labs are building RL Agents in 2026, I wrote a full article about it.

It covers the evolution from RLHF to GRPO with verifiable rewards and using an LLM-as-judge reward function. This idea extends RL training to non-verifiable agentic tasks without writing custom reward functions.

items.title: CEO OpenAI Sam Altman chốt định giá 1.250 tỷ USD, bên mua IPO Anthropic chỉ tính 1.100 tỷ – Martin Cid Magazine VN
items.summary:
Giờ là phép so sánh khiến vòng gọi vốn của OpenAI trở nên khó xử. Chỉ vài giờ trước tin tức về OpenAI, Bloomberg đưa tin một số nhà đầu tư tiềm năng mua cổ phiếu IPO của Anthropic cho rằng công ty có thể chỉ đáng giá 1,1 nghìn tỷ USD, thấp hơn mức khoảng 2 nghìn tỷ USD mà giới đầu tư được cho là kỳ vọng cách đó chừng một tháng. Anthropic muốn đạt mức định giá 1,5 nghìn tỷ USD. Theo The Wall Street Journal, một số nhà đầu tư hiện hữu của công ty không cho rằng con số đó thực tế, và một cổ đông [...] Theo những thông tin Bloomberg đưa tin đầu tiên, sau đó được TechCrunch, SiliconANGLE và The Decoder đăng lại, OpenAI đã huy động 11 tỷ USD trong vòng gọi vốn định giá công ty ở mức 1,25 nghìn tỷ USD. Các nhà đầu tư chuyển tiền vào thứ Sáu. Vòng gọi vốn vẫn chưa khép lại. OpenAI tiếp tục tìm kiếm thêm vốn, và tổng số tiền có thể lên khoảng 20 tỷ USD trong những tuần tới. Hồi tháng 3, công ty huy động 122 tỷ USD với mức định giá 852 tỷ USD, vì thế mức định giá mới cao hơn khoảng 47%. [...] Đó mới là diễn biến ẩn sau tin tức. Sam Altman đã nói rõ OpenAI không vội lên sàn. Anthropic thì đi theo hướng ngược lại. Một trong hai công ty sắp được định giá bởi những người xa lạ, có thể bán cổ phiếu ngay sáng hôm sau. Công ty còn lại vừa được định giá bởi những người vốn đã sở hữu một phần doanh nghiệp.
